# release: homebrew: keep the Formula without a deprecation

## Motivation

v0.2.0 published the Formula with `deprecate! date: "2026-11-05", because: "is replaced by the cask", replacement_cask: "maintainer"`. From that date `brew install` and `brew upgrade` of the Formula warn that it is replaced by the Cask and point users to it. The direction has changed: v0.3.0 makes the Formula the only Homebrew channel, because only a Formula can carry the local service that `brew services` runs ([[MAIN-125]]). Until then, v0.2.x keeps publishing both the Formula and the Cask, and neither of them may push users to the other. A v0.2.x release before 2026-11-05 lifts the deprecation.

## PoC

```bash
$ make go-dist-check && grep -c 'deprecate!' dist/homebrew/Formula/maintainer.rb
0
$ brew upgrade --formula octolab/tap/maintainer   # after the patch: no "has been deprecated" warning
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Formula generated by `make go-dist-check` has no `deprecate!`, and its caveat says only that maintainer is published as a Formula and as a Cask and that one installation is enough, without recommending either.
- [ ] The Cask is generated and published as before.
- [ ] `make release-config-check` accepts exactly the `brews` deprecation and nothing else.
- [ ] README, Get started, AGENTS.md and the workflows guide present the Formula and the Cask as two ways to install the same release and say nothing about retiring the Formula.
- [ ] The release with this change is published before 2026-11-05.

## Out of scope

Retiring the Cask, the local service and the one-Formula channel of v0.3.0 ([[MAIN-125]]); the published v0.2.0 note.
